title: Business
about: Collocations for talking about business: starting a firm, making a profit or a loss, going under, competition, contracts and deals, such as set up a business, stiff competition and do business.

parts.title: Common mistakes
parts.note: Справи ведуть з do, а не з make: do business (with sb) — We do a lot of business with hotels. Make натомість працює з грошима, які заробив чи втратив: make a profit, make a loss. У таблиці — ще кілька пасток, коли говориш про бізнес.

items.pattern: go into business (with sb) · go into business as a plumber / florist… · go – went – gone
items.meaning: start your own company or start working for yourself
items.example: After twenty years as a chef, Marta **went into business** with her sister and opened a café.
more: My uncle **went into business** as a plumber when he was only twenty-two.
We'd love to **go into business** together one day, but neither of us has any savings.
items.watchOut: «Зайнятися бізнесом» — go into business, без артикля і не make business. Go into business — почати свою справу, а do business — вести справи з кимось (див. b10).

items.pattern: set up / start (up) a business / company / firm · set up – set up – set up · formal: establish a company
items.meaning: create a new company and get it started
items.example: My neighbour **set up a cake business** in her own kitchen, and now she bakes for half the town.
more: It took them a year to save enough money to **set up their own business**.
My grandfather **set up the family firm** in 1968 with just one van.
items.watchOut: «Відкрити (організувати) свою справу» — set up / start a business, а не organise a business чи make a firm. Про конкретний магазин або кафе кажуть і open: They opened a café.

items.pattern: go into partnership (with sb) · be in partnership with sb · a business partner
items.meaning: join another person so that you own and run a business together
items.uk: стати компаньйонами, об'єднатися для спільної справи
items.example: After two years on her own, she **went into partnership** with her brother-in-law, and they opened a second shop.
more: My dad and his brother **went into partnership** and opened a fish and chip shop.
Think carefully before you **go into partnership** with a relative.
items.watchOut: Зазвичай без артикля: go into partnership. Прийменник — with: with my cousin, а не to my cousin.

items.pattern: make a (small / big / healthy) profit · make a profit of £500 · make a profit on sth
items.meaning: earn more money than you spend
items.example: The beach café **made a healthy profit** during the hot summer.
more: If you buy old chairs cheaply and repaint them, you can **make a profit** of fifty pounds a chair.
It took the bakery three years to **make a profit**.
items.watchOut: «Отримати прибуток» — make a profit, а не receive a profit; get a profit теж звучить неприродно. Протилежне — make a loss.

items.pattern: make a (small / big / huge) loss · make a loss on sth · ≠ make a profit · AmE often: lose money
items.meaning: spend more money than you earn
items.example: The bookshop **made a loss** because the rent went up twice in one year.
more: Many farmers **made a loss** on their potatoes this year because prices were so low.
The football club **made a loss** of £20,000 last season.
items.watchOut: «Працювати в мінус» — make a loss, а не work in minus і не get a loss.

items.pattern: a business / firm / shop goes under · go – went – gone · informal
items.meaning: fail financially and have to close
items.example: When the factory closed, half the shops in our village **went under**.
more: The travel agency **went under**, and lots of people lost the money they'd paid for their holidays.
Without a loan from the bank, the farm would have **gone under**.
items.watchOut: «Прогоріти» — go under, а не burn out: burn out — вигоріти, виснажитися від роботи.

items.pattern: a business / firm / magazine / club folds · no object
items.meaning: closes because it is failing and has no money
items.example: The little theatre in our town **folded** after the council stopped giving it money.
more: Lots of new restaurants **fold** within their first year.
My uncle's printing business **folded** in the nineties, so he became a taxi driver.
items.watchOut: Тут fold — про бізнес, а не «складати» (fold the clothes). Дієслово без додатка: The shop folded, а не was folded.

items.pattern: go bankrupt · be declared bankrupt · bankruptcy · also informal: go bust, go broke
items.meaning: be unable to pay your debts, so a court takes control of what you own
items.example: The holiday company **went bankrupt**, and thousands of tourists were stuck abroad.
more: My great-grandfather **went bankrupt** in the 1930s and lost his farm.
If the restaurant doesn't pay its suppliers, it could **go bankrupt**.
items.watchOut: Bankrupt тут — прикметник, тому go bankrupt (як go grey, go mad). Не кажи «The firm bankrupted»: дієслово bankrupt означає «розорити когось». Наголос на першому складі.

items.pattern: win / get / be awarded a contract (to do sth) · ≠ lose a contract · sign a contract
items.meaning: be chosen by a customer to do a particular job or supply goods
items.example: Our local bakery **won a contract** to make sandwiches for the hospital café.
more: A family firm from our village **won the contract** to look after the park.
The bus company **won a contract** to take children to school.
items.watchOut: «Виграти контракт (тендер)» — win a contract, а не achieve чи reach a contract: reach кажуть про домовленість (reach an agreement). У розмові можна й get a contract.

items.pattern: stiff / fierce / tough competition (for sth / from sb) · face stiff competition
items.meaning: competition that is very strong and hard to beat
items.example: There's **stiff competition** for customers on our high street: there are five cafés in a row.
more: Small farm shops face **stiff competition** from the big supermarkets.
The village garage has **stiff competition** now that a big one has opened on the main road.
items.watchOut: «Жорстка конкуренція» — stiff / fierce / tough competition, а не rigid чи cruel competition. Strong competition теж кажуть, а hard competition звучить менш природно.

items.pattern: take on staff / workers / an assistant · take sb on · take – took – taken · also hire / recruit staff
items.meaning: start employing new people
items.uk: наймати працівників, брати людей на роботу
items.example: The garden centre **takes on extra staff** every spring.
more: Business is going well, so we're going to **take on** two more waiters.
The new hotel will **take on** about forty local people.
items.watchOut: «Брати на роботу» — take sb on, а не take sb to work: це «підвезти когось на роботу». Staff — збірне слово без -s: two new members of staff, а не two new staffs.

items.pattern: create / provide jobs (for sb) · job creation
items.meaning: make new jobs available for people
items.example: The new factory will **create two hundred jobs** in the area.
more: Small family firms **create jobs** in places where big companies never go.
Opening a second shop will **create five new jobs**.
items.watchOut: «Робочі місця» — просто jobs, а не working places. Workplace — це місце, де працюєш: офіс, цех, магазин.

items.pattern: sales figures improve / rise / fall · sales figures are up / down · monthly / annual sales figures
items.meaning: numbers that show how much a business has sold
items.example: Our **sales figures** for December were the best we've ever had.
more: The shop's **sales figures** fell when the road outside was closed for repairs.
Every Monday the manager pins last week's **sales figures** on the staff noticeboard.
items.watchOut: «Продажі» — sales, у множині: Sales are up. Тому sales figures, а не selling figures чи sale figures. Figures тут — цифри, а не фігури.

items.pattern: an annual turnover of £… · have a turnover of £…
items.meaning: the total amount of money a business takes from sales in a year
items.example: The garage is a small family firm with an **annual turnover** of about half a million pounds.
more: The café has an **annual turnover** of £200,000, but most of that goes on rent and wages.
Their **annual turnover** has doubled since they started selling abroad.
items.watchOut: Turnover — оборот, тобто всі гроші від продажів, а не прибуток: profit — те, що лишається після витрат. Не плутай з takeover — поглинання (купівля) однієї компанії іншою.

items.pattern: the secret of / to sb's success · the secret of a happy marriage / good bread…
items.meaning: the special reason why someone or something does well
items.example: Fresh bread baked every morning is **the secret of their success**.
more: A good location is **the secret of success** for most cafés.
Friendly staff are **the secret to our success**.
items.watchOut: Перед secret стоїть the: the secret of success, а не secret of success. Після secret — of або to: the secret of / to our success.

items.pattern: carry out / do / conduct market research (into sth) · conduct is formal · research is uncountable
items.meaning: collect information about what customers want and what they will buy
items.example: Before opening the pet shop, we **carried out market research** to see how many people in the area had dogs.
more: The bakery **conducted market research** by asking customers to fill in a short questionnaire.
You should **carry out some market research** before you spend money on a shop.
items.watchOut: Research незлічуване: some market research, а не a market research чи researches. «Провести дослідження» — carry out / conduct / do research, а не make research.

items.pattern: launch a (new) product / range / service · a product launch
items.meaning: start selling a new product and tell people about it
items.example: The tea company is **launching a new product**: herbal tea for children.
more: The brewery **launched a new range** of alcohol-free beers in the spring.
It costs a lot of money to **launch a new product**, especially on television.
items.watchOut: «Запустити новий товар» — launch a product, а не start чи run a product. Вимова: /lɔːntʃ/, як lawn + ch.

items.pattern: (good / excellent) after-sales service · also customer service
items.meaning: the help a shop or company gives customers after they buy something, such as repairs and advice
items.example: We bought our washing machine from a small local shop because their **after-sales service** is excellent.
more: Good **after-sales service** keeps customers coming back.
The bike was cheap, but there was no **after-sales service** when it broke.

items.pattern: run a business / shop / café / hotel / farm · run – ran – run
items.meaning: be in charge of a business and organise how it works
items.example: My parents **run a small hotel** by the sea.
more: **Running a business** means you never really have a day off.
She **runs the family farm** with her two brothers.
items.watchOut: «Тримати кафе», «вести свою справу» — run a café / a business, а не hold a café. Lead кажуть хіба про керівника великої компанії чи команди, а про магазин чи кафе — run.

items.pattern: float a company (on the stock market / stock exchange) · be floated
items.meaning: start selling shares in a company to the public for the first time
items.example: The family that started the supermarket chain finally decided to **float the company** in 1995.
more: They plan to **float the company on the stock market** to raise money for new shops.
When the airline was **floated**, thousands of ordinary people bought shares.
items.watchOut: Float тут — не «плавати», а вперше виставити акції компанії на продаж. Біржа — the stock market / the stock exchange.

items.pattern: a company goes public · go – went – gone
items.meaning: start selling shares in a company to the public for the first time
items.uk: вийти на біржу, стати публічною компанією
items.example: The garden centre chain **went public** last year, and its shares sold out in a day.
more: When a company **goes public**, anyone can buy its shares.
The football club **went public** in the 1990s, and many fans bought shares.
items.watchOut: Go public (with sth) має й інше значення — розповісти всім про щось приховане: She went public with her story.

items.pattern: cease trading · formal; informal: close down, stop trading
items.meaning: stop doing business and close
items.example: A sign on the door said the shop had **ceased trading** and thanked customers for twenty years of support.
more: The little airline **ceased trading** last month, leaving hundreds of passengers without flights.
When the owners retired, the family firm **ceased trading** after ninety years.
items.watchOut: Cease — формальне слово для оголошень і новин; у розмові кажуть close down або stop trading. Читається /siːs/, римується з peace.

items.pattern: cut-throat competition · a cut-throat business / world
items.meaning: extremely fierce competition where businesses will do almost anything to win
items.example: There's **cut-throat competition** between the pizza takeaways in our town: one even gives away free garlic bread.
more: The two ferry companies were in **cut-throat competition**, so tickets cost almost nothing.
Fashion is a **cut-throat business**.
items.watchOut: «Жорстока конкуренція» — cut-throat або fierce competition, а не cruel competition: cruel кажуть про людей і вчинки, які навмисно завдають болю.

items.pattern: market forces · leave sth to market forces
items.meaning: the way supply and demand, not the government, decide prices and which businesses survive
items.example: When lots of people want to live in an area, **market forces** push rents up.
more: Farmers say **market forces** have pushed the price of milk too low.
**Market forces** mean that shops which don't change with the times slowly disappear.

items.pattern: go out of business · put sb out of business
items.meaning: stop trading because the business has failed
items.example: The video rental shop **went out of business** years ago; now it's a nail bar.
more: The dry cleaner's **went out of business** because fewer people wear suits now.
The family toy shop **went out of business** after sixty years.
items.watchOut: Без артикля і з of: go out of business, а не go out from business. Поруч — put sb out of business: довести когось до закриття.

items.pattern: business is booming · a booming business / town
items.meaning: trade is going extremely well
items.example: Since the heatwave started, **business has been booming** at the ice cream kiosk.
more: When it rains in London, **business is booming** for umbrella sellers.
The town has lots of young families now, so **business is booming** for the toy shop.
items.watchOut: Тут business — незлічуване «справи, торгівля», тому без артикля: Business is booming. «Процвітає» — booming або thriving, а не flowering.

items.pattern: a rival company / firm / shop / brand · a rival = a competitor
items.meaning: a company that competes with another one for the same customers
items.example: Our chemist lowered its prices when a **rival company** opened a shop next door.
more: The two **rival cafés** on the square are owned by brothers who don't speak to each other.
When her usual supplier put its prices up, she started buying coffee beans from a **rival firm**.
items.watchOut: «Конкурент» — a rival або a competitor. Concurrent означає «одночасний», конкурента так не називають. Вимова: /ˈraɪvl/, з «ай».

items.pattern: do / strike / make a deal (with sb) · do sb a deal · It's a deal!
items.meaning: make a business agreement with someone
items.example: The farm shop **struck a deal** with a local dairy to sell its cheese.
more: We finally **did a deal** with the landlord: lower rent in return for a five-year lease.
The football club **did a deal** with a local brewery to sell its beer at matches.
items.watchOut: «Укласти угоду» — do / strike / make a deal, а не lay чи put a deal. A good deal — ще й вигідна покупка: I got a good deal on this car.

items.pattern: balance the / your budget · balance the books
items.meaning: make sure you don't spend more money than you have
items.example: The village shop only **balanced its budget** because volunteers worked for free.
more: The school had to cancel some trips to **balance the budget**.
Every January we sit down at the kitchen table and try to **balance the family budget**.
items.watchOut: «Звести бюджет» — balance the budget, а не close чи weigh the budget. Вимова: /ˈbʌdʒɪt/, з «а», не «бюджет».

items.pattern: put in / make / submit a bid (for sth / to do sth) · a bid of £…
items.meaning: offer to do a job or buy something for a particular price
items.uk: подати пропозицію (заявку на тендер), запропонувати ціну
items.example: My uncle's firm **put in a bid** to paint all the classrooms at the primary school.
more: We **put in a bid** of £300,000 for the house, but someone offered more.
If you want the cleaning contract, you need to **put in a bid** by Friday.
items.watchOut: Bid — пропозиція ціни на тендері чи аукціоні. Заявку на роботу чи навчання подають інакше: apply for a job, make an application.

items.pattern: do business (with sb / in a place) · do a lot of business · business is uncountable here
items.meaning: buy, sell or work with someone as part of your trade
items.example: We've **done business** with the same flour supplier for fifteen years.
more: It's a pleasure to **do business** with you.
Lots of small firms in our town **do business** with hotels and restaurants.
items.watchOut: «Вести справи (бізнес)» — do business, а не make business. Business тут без артикля: do business with sb.

warmup.uk: Мій дядько тримає кав'ярню біля вокзалу.
warmup.q: My uncle ___ a café near the station.
warmup.explain: Тримати кафе, вести бізнес — run a café / a business. Hold і lead тут не підходять.

warmup.uk: Ми вже багато років співпрацюємо з цим постачальником.
warmup.q: We've ___ business with this supplier for years.
warmup.explain: Вести справи з кимось — do business with sb, а не make business.

warmup.uk: Цього року кав'ярня вперше отримала прибуток.
warmup.q: This year the coffee shop ___ a profit for the first time.
warmup.explain: Отримати прибуток — make a profit. Receive a profit — калька.

warmup.uk: Фірма таксі мого дядька прогоріла вже через два роки.
warmup.q: My uncle's taxi firm ___ after just two years.
warmup.explain: Прогоріти — go under (або go bankrupt). Дієслово bankrupt означає «розорити когось», тому The firm bankrupted — помилка; fall down — упасти. Burn out — вигоріти від утоми, про фірму так не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Новий супермаркет створить п'ятдесят робочих місць.
warmup.q: The new supermarket will create fifty ___.
warmup.explain: Робочі місця — jobs. Workplace — саме місце роботи: офіс, цех.

warmup.q: A ___ bakery has opened across the road.
warmup.explain: Конкурент — a rival (або a competitor). Concurrent означає «одночасний».

warmup.uk: На Різдво ми беремо на роботу ще трьох продавців.
warmup.q: At Christmas we ___ three more shop assistants.
warmup.explain: Наймати людей — take on staff. Take sb to work — підвезти когось на роботу.

warmup.uk: Ми домовилися із сусідньою кав'ярнею: вони продаватимуть наші торти.
warmup.q: We've ___ a deal with the café next door: they'll sell our cakes.
warmup.explain: Укласти угоду — do / strike / make a deal. «Укласти» тут не lay.

A.q: Last year the chemist's took £800,000 from customers, before paying any bills: that's its annual ___.
A.explain: Turnover — усі гроші від продажів за рік (оборот). Profit — те, що лишається після витрат, takeover — поглинання іншої компанії.

A.q: The language school ___ bankrupt, and the students never got their fees back.
A.explain: Go bankrupt — збанкрутувати. Bankrupt тут прикметник, як у go grey.

A.q: My cousin's building firm has ___ a contract to repair the church roof.
A.explain: Виграти (отримати) контракт — win a contract, у розмові ще get a contract. Reach — про домовленість: reach an agreement.

B.q: The new station has brought lots of commuters, and business is ___ at the café opposite.
B.explain: Business is booming — справи йдуть чудово.

B.q: With ___ competition from the big chains, it's hard for a small shoe shop to survive.
B.explain: Нещадна конкуренція — cut-throat (або fierce) competition. Cruel — жорстокий (про людей і вчинки), rigid — жорсткий, негнучкий (про правила, матеріали).

B.q: My dad never ___ business with people he doesn't trust.
B.explain: Вести справи з кимось — do business with sb, а не make business.

example.title: The bakery on Mill Street
example.uk:
Десять років тому моя тітка Роза відкрила маленьку пекарню на Млиновій вулиці, а через рік стала компаньйонкою свого сусіда Тома. Спочатку вони працювали в мінус, а коли неподалік відкрився супермаркет, ми всі думали, що пекарня прогорить.

Тоді Роза провела невелике дослідження ринку й дізналася, що людям бракує справжнього житнього хліба. Вона почала його пекти, і незабаром справи пішли чудово. Минулої весни пекарня виграла контракт на постачання хліба великому готелю, і Роза взяла на роботу ще двох пекарів.

Тепер вони щороку отримують прибуток і співпрацюють із половиною кав'ярень у місті. Коли Розу питають про секрет її успіху, вона лише всміхається й каже: «Вставайте о четвертій».
example.en:
Ten years ago my aunt Rosa [[set up|a2]] a small bakery on Mill Street, and a year later she [[went into partnership|a3]] with her neighbour Tom. At first they [[made a loss|a5]], and when a supermarket opened nearby, we all thought the bakery would [[go under|a6]].

Then Rosa [[carried out some market research|a16]] and learnt that people wanted proper rye bread. She started baking it, and soon [[business was booming|b5]]. Last spring the bakery [[won a contract|a9]] to supply bread to a big hotel, and Rosa [[took on|a11]] two more bakers.

Now they [[make a profit|a4]] every year and [[do business|b10]] with half the cafés in town. When people ask about [[the secret of her success|a15]], Rosa just smiles and says, 'Get up at four.'
